messages.subject: labeling groups in a plot
parts:
Hi Everybody, 

I am having trouble labeling groups. I want the groups to be labeled, 1 label per MALE. 

Using the attached data set of random numbers "Random.csv". 

> library(ggplot2)
> library(Hmisc)
> r <- read.csv (file.choose (), header=T)
> r1 <- qplot (TREAT, RAND, data = r, stat="summary", fun.y = "mean" , group = MALE, color = MALE, width = 1.5)
> r2<-r1+stat_summary(fun.y = mean, geom = "line", aes(group= MALE,TREAT), size=1)
> r2
I would like to put labels for the 9 males (labeled 1-9), next to the right point of each line. Each line connects the mean of each male under two treatments. 

Label aesthetics seems to add a label for each of the 270 data points. 

Thank you for any help, 

Ackley

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: labeling groups in a plot
parts:
Hi:

Here's one way you can do it. The trick is to make both TREAT and RAND numeric and then adjust some labels at the end. I don't like using qplot() for this type of thing so I'm using the ggplot() approach which affords more control of where to define the aesthetics.
After creating the data frame r from your supplied data set,

library(ggplot2)
r <- read.csv("random.csv", header = TRUE)

# Create numeric versions of TREAT and RAND
r$treat <- as.numeric(r$TREAT)
r$rand <- as.numeric(r$RAND)

# Plot with numeric versions of TREAT and RAND. This makes it easier
# to add text labels later.
p <- ggplot(r) +
       stat_summary(fun.y = mean, geom = "point",
                    aes(x = treat, y = rand, group = MALE, color = MALE), 
                    width = 1.5) +

aes(x = treat, y = rand, group = MALE, color = MALE),
                    size = 1)

# Pull out the data used to create the ggplot p and select only
# those observations associated with x = 2 because that is the
# reference point for positioning the labels.

u <- ggplot_build(p)
v <- subset(u$data[[1]], x == 2)
v
str(v)

# Two vectors to tweak the x and y-positions of the text labels.
# I did this to separate the three labels at the bottom, which
# would overlap without the adjustment. I did it this way to 
# make it easier for you to adjust them yourself if you wished,
# or not use them at all. On a data set with many more groups,
# this may not be a good approach - see the directlabels package
# for a probably better alternative.

adjx <- c(0, -0.05, rep(0, 7))
adjy <- c(-0.2, 0, 0.2, rep(0, 6))

# Add the text labels to the graphic and then adjust the x-axis
# labels and the x-extent of the graph.

p + geom_text(data = v, aes(x = 2.1 + adjx, y = y + adjy, 
                            label = LETTERS[group])) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2), labels = c("A", "B")) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.5, 2.5))

There's a more elegant way of doing this using the gtables package, but this is a Q & D method. Another point is that with text labels for each MALE, the legend is basically superfluous, so to remove it, add

   scale_x_discrete(guide = "none")


Dennis

messages.subject: Re: labeling groups in a plot
parts:
Hi Again, 

Just to say, I found that the directlabels package is able to do this. 

add
> library (directlabels)
and after making the plot, 
> direct.label ( PlotName , list ( "last.qp" , hjust=-1 ,vjust=0 ,cex=1 ))

Thanks again for the input, 

Cheers, 

Ackley
